input.description: User-supplied case summary and AI-generated statutory analysis; leads, not authority.

curiosity_follow_up.scope: Targeted review of current legislation, leading and later appellate authority, legislative history and original academic research; not an exhaustive search of every prosecution.
corrections: G and J paragraph 83 expressly declines to determine curiosity in the abstract; the supplied categorical no-defence claim is not adopted.
Dunleavy illustrates mixed purposes and withdrawing an incapable defence from the jury, not a blanket ban on curiosity.
Section 58(3A) does not expressly require institutional affiliation, peer review or ethics approval; this is not a promise that private reading qualifies as academic research.
Material need not be useful exclusively to terrorists; ordinary maps and timetables are examples of the limit, not an exemption for every dual-use reference book.
Dinesson's assessment of practice is distinguished from the legal rule; six qualitative interviews do not establish an acquittal probability.
No conclusion about the user's circumstances and no manufactured-excuse checklist.
curiosity_follow_up.source_access: Dunleavy and current sections 58/118 read from official XML; G and J from Parliament's judgment PDF; Hansard and Cambridge University Press read directly.

corrections: Section 58 reasonable-excuse examples are in 58(3A)(a) and (b)(i)-(ii), not 3B/3C.
Section 118 imposes an evidential burden; the prosecution must disprove the defence beyond reasonable doubt once sufficiently raised.
No automatic title-based liability or claim that the offence is strict liability.
Bel: corrected citation to [2021] EWCA Crim 1461; physical book and December 2018 Amazon purchase recorded in judgment, not an electronic-copy assumption.
John: corrected citation to [2022] EWCA Crim 54; six acquittals retained; appellate reasoning includes unlawful sentence structure.
Howarth: original 54-month custodial term reduced to 45 months on 24 November 2022; additional one-year licence retained.
Walker and Creagh: acquittals do not reveal jurors' reasoning or establish universal exemptions.
Cristea: distinguish possession conviction from police account of suspected attack planning in the wider group.
Smith: use 2017 as recorded in the Independent Reviewer's note rather than supplied 2016 date.
Amazon availability is supported as a dated claim, not certified current stock or edition identity.
